resources.string: Synthetic chat notifications for testing notification readers
Group name — leave empty for a 1:1 chat
Append a counter to each new message

Dates the message into the past while the notification still posts now, the way delivery latency or an offline backlog looks. Readers that stamp messages with the arrival time cannot tell; readers that use the sender\'s time can.
Two places a chat app can put the sender picture. Turn on one at a time to see which one the reading app picks up: blue L = largeIcon, orange P = Person icon.
…but withhold it from the next message posted

Keeps the icon on messages already in the conversation and omits it from new ones — what a group member whose avatar has not downloaded looks like. A reader that falls back to an earlier entry will show the wrong person\'s picture.

The intent an \"open original app\" button fires. On Android 14+ both the creator and the sender must allow the background activity start; the picker below controls the creator half. Android 16 replaced ALLOWED with two narrower modes, so all three are offered — anything the device is too old for is downgraded and noted in the event log.

Lets the system remove the notification when it is tapped, which is the only way to produce REASON_CLICK for a listener watching removals. Needs the contentIntent above, since the tap is what triggers it. Off by default: most chat apps leave the flag off and clear their own notification once the chat opens, which arrives as REASON_APP_CANCEL instead.
How chats are spread over ids and tags

Decides the shape of sbn.key, which is user|package|id|tag|uid. A reader that remembers a key so it can act on it later behaves differently against each shape, and the difference only shows up on apps that use it. These three were measured from real notifications.
Post a group summary beside the chats

Posts a summary notification over the chats, refreshed whenever one is posted and then left alone — it is never updated or removed when a chat\'s notification goes away. That is the point: it makes visible whether the system takes an orphaned summary down by itself, which decides whether a reader that cancels a chat has to clean up after it.
Rebuild puts a chat back under a new id

Only applies to the rebuild above. The chat returns under a notification id it has never had, so anything that remembered the old key is left holding one that names nothing. None of the clients measured here does this — their per-chat ids are stable — so this is for finding out what would happen if one did.

Which group the chat joins, and so which summary covers it. Two different names puts two groups in the shade at once, which is the only way to check that clearing everything under one of them leaves the other one\'s summary standing. Not the same thing as the group chat name above: that one names a conversation, this one names a bundle of notifications.
Adds a RemoteInput action. Replies land in the event log below, which also records whether the notification was still showing at the time.
Cancel the notification after a reply arrives
Rebuild all notifications after a reply arrives

A rebuild cancels every notification this app has posted, then posts back the ones still unread. Telegram-based clients do this on every reply — the chat replied to is marked read and does not return. For a moment the app has nothing showing, which is what a reader must not mistake for "the user has dealt with all of this". The gap below is how long that moment lasts.
Echo my reply back into the notification

What happens when neither of the two above applies: the reply you just sent is appended to the conversation and the notification is posted again, which is how a client that shows your sent message behaves. Turn it off to leave the shade untouched after a reply — the only setting here under which a reading app\'s own cancellation is the only thing that can change it.

An album sends several messages that all claim the same send time, one notification update each, the way a batch of photos arrives. With the counter off the texts match too and only one should be recorded; with it on they differ and all of them should survive.
Re-posting keeps the same notification id and the same message list — the refresh pattern that trips duplicate detection in reading apps.
Give the unchanged message a fresh timestamp on re-post
Reaching this screen means the intent was allowed to launch. If a reading app\'s open button does nothing, the launch was blocked before it got here.
Notification permission is required to post test notifications
